ABSTRACT: Despite the synthetic versatility of difluorocarbene, its high reactivity severely regulates widespread applications of
difluorocarbene in organic synthesis. Here, we report a copper difluorocarbene-involved catalytic coupling, representing a new mode
of the difluoromethylation reaction. This method allows difluoromethylation of a wide range of readily available allyl/propargyl
electrophiles with NaBH
3
CN and low-cost difluorocarbene precursor BrCF
2
CO
2
K, featuring high cost-efficiency, high stereo- and
regioselectivities, and high functional group tolerance, even with complex drug-like molecules. Applying the method led to the
efficient synthesis of deuterated difluoromethylated compounds of medicinal interest. The resulting difluoromethylated allyl and
allenyl products can serve as versatile synthons for diverse transformations, rendering the approach attractive for synthesizing
complex fluorinated structures. Experimental mechanistic studies and computational calculations reveal that the formation of a
difluoromethylcopper(I) intermediate through the nucleophilic attack of boron hydride on the copper(I) difluorocarbene is the key
step in the reaction.
■
INTRODUCTION
Difluorocarbene has received increasing attention due to its
synthetic versatility in forming two bonds to its carbon
centers.
1
This distinct property significantly expands the
chemical space to construct new fluorinated structures for
modern drug discovery
2
and advanced functional materials.
3
However, the high reactivity of difluorocarbene severely
regulates its widespread synthetic applications. As a result,
the reaction types of difluorocarbene are very limited.
3a,4
Using
metal to modulate the reactivity of difluorocarbene is a
promising strategy to overcome this limitation. In this context,
efforts have been made to synthesize and characterize metal
difluorocarbene complexes over the past 40 years.
5
However,
the use of metal difluorocarbene complexes for catalytic
synthesis remains a long-standing challenge due to the lack of
catalytic reactivity of the isolated metal difluorocarbene
complexes.
5,6
Recently, we developed a palladium difluorocarbene-
involved catalytic coupling,
7

difluorocarbene with aryl borons/alkynes and proton.

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Optimization of the Reaction Conditions. To test our
hypothesis, initially, we chose readily available branched allyl
acetate 1a as the model substrate and low-cost BrCF
2
CO
2
K 2
as the difluorocarbene precursor. After extensive efforts using
various hydride sources, including silanes and boron hydrides,
we failed to achieve the desired product 3a (Table S1).
Replacing the acetate group with a more reactive leaving
group, trifluoroacetate, benefits the reaction efficiency (Table
1). A 25% yield of linear difluoromethylated product 3a was
obtained when the reaction mixture of 1b (1.0 equiv) and 2
(2.0 equiv) was treated with triethylsilane (Et
3
SiH, 1.5 equiv)
and K
3
PO
4
in the presence of CuCl (10 mol %) and 1,10-phen
L1 (10 mol %) in MeCN at 50 °C (entry 1). A survey of the
hydride sources (entries 2−6) showed NaBH
3
CN was the
optimal choice, providing 3a in 73% yield with high
stereoselectivity (E/Z = 15:1) without observation of branched
product 3a′ (entry 6). The reaction was not sensitive to the
ligand, as phen-, bpy-, and NHC-based ligands produced 3a
(entries 7−13). Proper steric ligand 2,9-diMe-1,10-phen L2
could improve the yield to 82% with an excellent E/Z ratio (E/
Z >99:1, entry 7). The comparable yields were also obtained
using 2,9-diPh-1,10-phen L6 (76%, entry 11), 2,2′-bpy L8
(84%, entry 13), and IMes L9 (82%, entry 14), with slightly
lower E/Z ratios observed. However, bidentate phosphine
ligands, such as Xantphos and DPEphos, diminished the yields
(Table S4). Finally, decreasing the reaction concentration and
using 5 mol % CuCl could provide 3a in 85% isolated yield (E/
Z >99:1, entry 15). Linear trifluoroacetate 1b′ was also
applicable to the reaction, with a lower yield (35%) obtained
(entry 16), probably due to the easier oxidative addition of
copper(I) with branched allyl trifluoroacetates 1b via an S
N
2′
oxidative addition pathway.
15
No product was observed
without copper salt (entry 17). Yet the absence of ligand
provided 3a in good yield (68%) with lower E/Z selectivity
(E/Z = 16:1, entry 18), demonstrating the essential role of
copper salt in promoting the reaction.
Substrate Scope Analysis and Synthetic Applications.
With the viable reaction conditions in hand, we examined the
substrate scope of this copper difluorocarbene-involved
catalytic difluoromethylation reaction (Scheme 2). Various
branched aliphatic allyl trifluoroacetates 1 underwent coupling
efficiently with excellent linear selectivity (3a−3i, 3n, 3r).
16
The length of the carbon side chain did not interfere with the
reaction efficiency; even the substrates bearing additional
alkene moiety (3b−3d) were competent coupling partners
without observation of [2 + 1] cycloaddition side products
generated between difluorocarbene and carbon−carbon double
bond.

In contrast
to linear aliphatic allyl trifluoroacetates 1′ that afforded their
corresponding products in low yields (3a, 3c), branched and
linear aromatic allyl trifluoroacetates were more reactive,
providing the difluoromethylated products in good yields (3j).
The reaction exhibited a high functional group tolerance.
Important synthetic handles, such as carboxylic acid ester (3e),
furan (3f), thiophene (3g), alkyne (3l), and aryl bromide
(3m), were compatible with the reaction conditions, offering
good opportunities for derivatization. Notably, substrates
derived from complex molecules, such as protected chiral
diol (3n), febuxostat (3o), sulbactam (3p), ciprofibrate (3q),
and carbohydrate (3r), were amenable to this copper-catalyzed
process, demonstrating the potential application of the current
approach in modern drug discovery. The reaction can also be
extended to allyl chlorides and bromides, as exemplified by the
efficient synthesis of 3h. Furthermore, the cyclic allyl
electrophile was also a suitable substrate, providing difluor-
omethylated product 3i efficiently. However, aryl and alkenyl
trifluoroacetates were not applicable to the reaction, which
would be addressed in the future.
The reaction was not restricted to allyl substrates, as
propargyl electrophiles were also suitable coupling partners
with L6 as the ligand, providing a wide range of
difluoromethylated allenes with high efficiency and selectivity
(Scheme 3). Although extensive efforts have been made in the
preparation of allenes,
17
scarce examples of efficient synthesis
of difluoromethylated allenes have been reported.
16b,18
Given
the synthetic versatility of allenes
17c−g
and the unique
properties of the difluoromethyl group in medicinal chemistry,
developing efficient methods to access these valuable
fluorinated structures is of great interest. We found that the
regioselectivity of the difluoromethylation could be controlled
by the propargyl substrates: branched propargyl sulfonates
provided “linear” products (6a−6k), while linear propargyl
sulfonates or chlorides afforded “branched” allenes as the
major products (7a−7d), thereby providing a synthetically
versatile route to difluoromethylated allenes. A range of

CONCLUSIONS
In summary, we have developed a new mode of catalytic
difluoromethylation reaction with low-cost and readily
available BrCF
2
CO
2
K and NaBH
3
CN as the difluoromethyl
source. The reaction allows difluoromethylation of various allyl
and propargyl electrophiles with high efficiency, featuring high
regio- and stereoselectivities and high functional group
tolerance, even with complex drug-like molecules. The use of
branched or linear propargyl electrophiles could regioselec-
tively control the structure of difluoromethylated allenes,
providing a facile route to access these valuable fluorinated
structures. Remarkably, the method can also be applied to the
preparation of medicinally interesting deuterated difluorome-
thylated compounds that otherwise are difficult to access
through conventional methods. The diverse transformations of
the resulting difluoromethylated products led to complex
fluorinated structures, showing the prospect of the current
approach in organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry.
Experimental mechanistic studies and DFT calculations reveal
that a [Cu
I
]�CF
2
species is involved in the reaction, and the
formation of the key intermediate [Cu
I
]−CF
2
H through the
nucleophilic attack of boron hydride to [Cu
I
]�CF
2
is
responsible for the current copper-catalyzed process. This
proof-of-concept study provides a new avenue for cost-
efficiently synthesizing difluoromethylated compounds and
advances the field of copper difluorocarbene chemistry.
